summary: self-certificates ships a base64-obfuscated dropper that fetches and executes remote Python
details: The package ships test/key.pem disguised as an RSA private key. index.js strips the PEM armor and base64-decodes the body into an executable JavaScript payload, then passes it as the third argument to selfsign.generate() from the companion dependency self-sign, which executes it. The decoded payload contains a second base64-encoded URL that resolves to https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php, fetches its response, and pipes it into a detached `python3 -` (or `python` on win32) child process with windowsHide, running arbitrary attacker-controlled Python on the host. Any consumer that invokes the package's certificate-generation API triggers remote code execution on their machine. The fake-PEM carrier under test/ and the double base64 layering (payload + C2 URL) exist solely to hide the dropper from casual review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
